Which of these four is the eldest?

Oliver Heaviside (born 1850) is the earliest of the four. Although at odds with the scientific establishment for most of his life, Heaviside changed the face of telecommunications, mathematics, and science.
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?

Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four. Originally specified in the late 1950s, it is the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use, after Fortran.
Which of these four appeared first?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Pierre Curie is a physicist. Pierre Curie (15 May 1859 – 19 April 1906) was a French physicist and chemist, and a pioneer in crystallography and magnetism.
Which of these four is a chemist?
Mario Molina is a chemist. Mario José Molina-Pasquel Henríquez (19 March 1943 – 7 October 2020) was a Mexican physical chemist.
What is the atomic number of Hydrogen?
Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
In what year was Ted Kaczynski born?
Ted Kaczynski: The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
In what year was Uranium discovered?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
In what year was Cobalt discovered?
Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Ciprofloxacin: Pfizer. Ciprofloxacin, sold under the brand name Cipro among others, is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat a number of bacterial infections.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25 from?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25: Soviet Union. Designed by the Soviet Union's Mikoyan-Gurevich bureau, it is an aircraft built primarily using stainless steel.
Who is credited with discovering Tucana?
Tucana: Petrus Plancius. Tucana (The Toucan) is a constellation in the southern sky, named after the toucan, a South American bird.
Who is credited with discovering Cro-Magnon?
Cro-Magnon: Louis Lartet. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Makemake?
Makemake: Michael E. Brown. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this family of hook-billed raptors includes buzzards, vultures, and kites across 75 genera — which family is this?
Accipitridae is one of the four families within the order Accipitriformes, and is a family of small to large birds of prey with strongly hooked bills and variable morphology based on diet.
This exaggerated immune reaction causes the body to mistake a harmless substance for a threat, triggering symptoms from a runny nose to a full anaphylactic reaction — what is it?
Allergy is an exaggerated immune response where the body mistakenly identifies an ordinarily harmless allergen as a threat.
Nicknamed the 'nail mosquito,' this genus — first classified in 1818 — is the sole mosquito genus known to carry human malaria — which genus is it?
Anopheles is a genus of mosquito first described by the German entomologist J. W. Meigen in 1818.
A methyl ester built from aspartic acid and phenylalanine, this non-saccharide sweetener is among the most-studied food additives ever, judged safe by over 100 regulatory bodies — what is it?
Aspartame is an artificial, non-saccharide sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.

Found naturally in many plants and abbreviated "Bz," this white crystalline compound is the simplest of the aromatic carboxylic acids and lends its salts to the world of food preservatives — what is it?
Benzoic acid is a white or colorless crystalline organic compound with the formula C6H5COOH, whose structure consists of a benzene ring (C6H6) with a carboxyl (C(=O)OH) substituent.
Unlike most elements, this one is made almost entirely by cosmic ray collisions rather than inside stars, making it rare despite its light atomic weight. What element is it (symbol B)?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is commonly spread on roads for de-icing and dust control, and its hygroscopic nature lets it pull moisture straight from the air — what compound is it?
Calcium chloride is an inorganic compound, a salt with the chemical formula CaCl2.
This usually bacterial infection of the skin's inner layers causes spreading redness, swelling, and pain, most often on the legs or face, sometimes accompanied by fever — what is it?
Cellulitis is usually a bacterial infection involving the inner layers of the skin. It specifically affects the dermis and subcutaneous fat.
Resembling an oversized lemon with a thick, coarse rind, this large fragrant citrus fruit is one of the original ancestors from which all other citrus varieties developed — which fruit?

Citron (Citrus medica) is a large fragrant citrus fruit with a thick, coarse rind. It is one of the original citrus fruits from which all other citrus types developed through natural hybrid speciation or artificial hybridization.
This inorganic compound's blue crystalline pentahydrate form was historically called blue vitriol, while its anhydrous form is white and dissolves in water to form an octahedral complex. What is it?
Copper(II) sulfate is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula CuSO4.
Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered photoelasticity and an angle that bears his name — and also improved the stereoscope. Who was he?
David Brewster (11 December 1781 - 10 February 1868) was a Scottish scientist, inventor, author, and academic administrator.
Charles Darwin spent years experimenting on these mucilage-coated plants, first proving that plants could be carnivorous — which genus of nearly 200 "sundew" species is it?
Drosera is commonly known as the sundews, is one of the largest genera of carnivorous plants, with at least 194 species.
This discipline systematically applies natural science and mathematics to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft under real-world constraints. What field is it?
Engineering is the practice of systematically applying natural science and mathematics to design and improve systems, devices, or processes that solve problems under constraints.
Home to seven living cat species, from the tiny black-footed cat to the jungle cat, and the wild ancestor line of the housecat, which genus of felines is this?
Felis is a genus of small and medium-sized cat species native to most of Africa and south of 60 latitude in Europe and Asia to Indochina.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.
A group 11 noble metal that forms a natural alloy called electrum with silver, this element takes its symbol from the Latin aurum — what is it?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
A Hollywood star of Algiers and Boom Town, this Austrian-American actress also co-invented a wartime radio guidance system — who was she?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 - January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.

This condition occurs when cerebrospinal fluid builds up in and around the brain, in babies causing a rapid increase in head size and in the elderly causing poor balance and mental decline — what condition is it?
Hydrocephalus is a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) builds up within and/or around the brain, which can cause pressure to increase in the skull.

This sudden bleeding into brain tissue or its ventricles is one of two major stroke categories, alongside the blockage-caused kind, and can trigger headache, one-sided weakness, or sudden speech and vision problems — what's the condition?
Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), also known as hemorrhagic stroke, is a sudden bleeding into the tissues of the brain (i.e., the parenchyma), into its ventricles, or both.
This English scientist's 1808 book proposed that elements consist of identical atoms combining in fixed whole-number ratios, laying the groundwork for modern atomic theory — who is he?
John Dalton (5 or 6 September 1766 - 27 July 1844) was an English chemist, physicist, and meteorologist whose work laid the foundations of modern atomic theory and stoichiometric chemistry.
Despite its name suggesting a root vegetable, this biennial cultivar of wild cabbage grows a swollen edible stem above ground and is related to broccoli, kale, and Brussels sprouts — what is it?
Kohlrabi (scientific name Brassica oleracea Gongylodes Group), also called German turnip or turnip cabbage, is a biennial vegetable, a low, stout cultivar of wild cabbage.
This genus of large-flowered bulb plants is prized in gardens worldwide but is highly toxic to cats. What genus is it?
Lilium is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
Members of the family Scombridae, these open-ocean fish sport forked tails and green-blue tiger stripes, often wintering in deep water after a coastal spawning run — what fish are they?
Mackerel is a common name applied to a number of different species of pelagic fish, mostly from the family Scombridae.
Raised in Wilmington, Delaware by Turkish immigrant parents, this cardiac surgeon co-founded a complementary-care center for heart patients before finding fame on television — who is he?

Mehmet Oz (mə-MET JENG-ghiz oz; born June 11, 1960), also known as Dr. Oz, is an American television presenter, physician, author, educator, and government official serving as the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) since 2025.
This New World songbird mimics the calls of other species, insects, and frogs, and serves as the state bird of five U.S. states — which bird?
Mockingbird are a group of New World passerine bird from the family Mimidae.

This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, attacking REM sleep with daytime drowsiness, sleep paralysis, and cataplexy — sudden episodes where muscle tone simply vanishes. What is it?
Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep-wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.
Belonging to the beech family and encompassing about 500 species across the Northern Hemisphere, this hardwood tree or shrub bears a distinctive nut held in a small cup — name the tree?
Oak is a hardwood tree or shrub in the genus Quercus of the beech family.
Its name comes from the Greek for "from everywhere" because it turns up in nearly all foods — and this B vitamin lets animals build coenzyme A for energy. Which vitamin is it?
Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is a B vitamin and an essential nutrient.

Fill in the blank: “____ (PD) is a benign, acquired penile connective tissue disease characterized by the occurrence of fibrotic plaques within the tunica albuginea - the dense elastic covering of the corpora cavernosa.”

Peyronie's disease (PD) is a benign, acquired penile connective tissue disease characterized by the occurrence of fibrotic plaques within the tunica albuginea - the dense elastic covering of the corpora cavernosa. The plaques cause abnormal curvature, pain, penile deformities (e.g., narrowing or indentation), and usually erectile dysfunction, particularly during erection.
Carrying minor-planet number 134340, this icy Kuiper-belt world has about one-sixth the Moon's mass and got demoted when astronomers rewrote the rules — what is it?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Originating in Central Asia despite widespread cultivation elsewhere, this is the most commonly grown species of a fuzzy-skinned stone fruit — what is its scientific name?
Prunus armeniaca is the most commonly cultivated apricot species.

Rooted in Minangkabau cooking, this dish slow-simmers meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — both a method and a meal across the Malacca Strait; what is it?

Rendang is a fried meat or dry curry made of meat stewed in coconut milk and spices, widely popular across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and the southern parts of the Philippines, where each version is considered local cuisine.
First identified in Wuhan, this positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus prompted the WHO to declare a global health emergency from January 2020 to May 2023 — what's its name?
SARS-CoV-2 (SARSCoV2) is a coronavirus that causes COVID-19, the respiratory illness responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic that began in late 2019.
Born into a Russian-Jewish family in Moscow and brought to the US at age six, which co-founder of Google served as president of Alphabet until 2019?
Sergey Brin (born August 21, 1973) is an American computer scientist and businessman who co-founded Google with Larry Page.
Mostly made from potato starch but also lurking in apples and berries, this slowly-metabolized sugar alcohol is an isomer of mannitol, differing only by one hydroxyl group's orientation — what is it?
Sorbitol is a sugar alcohol with a sweet taste which the human body metabolizes slowly.
First flown in 1967 with its crew sitting side by side under variable-sweep wings, this Soviet bomber earned the NATO codename 'Fencer' — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-24 (NATO reporting name: Fencer) is a supersonic, all-weather tactical bomber developed in the Soviet Union.
This vast domain of human practice — divided into visual, literary, and performing branches — lets people transmit values, ideas, and experiences across generations. What is it?
The arts are a vast range of human practices involving creative expression, storytelling, and cultural participation.

This invasive annual plant, native to warm regions of Eurasia and Africa but now found in North America and Australia, produces small woody burrs with sharp spines capable of piercing bare feet. What plant is this?
Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
First glimpsed in 1892 through tobacco-plant disease and counted as the most numerous biological entity on Earth, this submicroscopic agent can only replicate inside a living cell. What is it?
Virus is a submicroscopic infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism.
Making up just 1% of described fungal species, these single-celled eukaryotes reproduce by budding or fission and usually measure a mere 3–4 micrometers across — what are they?
Yeast is any species of fungus that grows primarily in a unicellular form and reproduces via budding or fission.
Caused by excess growth hormone after the body's growth plates have closed, this disorder first shows up as enlarged hands and feet before affecting the jaw and forehead — what condition is it?
Acromegaly: Human disease that results in excess growth of certain parts of the body.
Also called the Persian silk tree or mimosa tree, this flowering species in the pea family is native to Asia — what is it?

Albizia julibrissin: Species of plant. Albizia julibrissin, the Persian silk tree, pink silk tree, or mimosa tree, is a species of tree in the Fabaceae family, native to southwestern and eastern Asia.
Despite being named after a European bird for its reddish-orange breast, this thrush is the most abundant landbird on its continent, numbering some 370 million individuals — what is it?
American robin: Species of bird. The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.
Belonging to the suborder Vermilingua and closely related to sloths, these mammals include giant, silky, and tamandua species that feed almost exclusively on ants and termites — what are they called?
Anteater: Mammals known for eating ants and termites.
Native to eastern North America's wet woods and swamps, this shrub genus produces bitter 'chokeberries' that reached Scandinavia and Russia by the eighteenth century — what genus is this?

Aronia: Genus of plants (chokeberries). Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'that which is thought worthy,' which term denotes a statement accepted as true without proof, serving as a starting point for further reasoning?
Axiom: Statement that is taken to be true.
A largely self-taught naturalist and astronomer born to a free mother in Maryland, he helped survey the District of Columbia and corresponded with Thomas Jefferson — who was he?
Benjamin Banneker: American scientist, surveyor and farmer (1731–1806)
Believed to descend from hounds once kept at a Belgian abbey, this scent hound can follow a human trail days old and is a favorite of police tracking escaped prisoners — which breed is it?
Bloodhound: Dog breed used for tracking by scent.
Grown on one of the Amazon's largest and longest-lived trees, this selenium-rich edible seed comes in a shell weighing up to 2 kilograms combined with its fruit. What is it?
Brazil nut: Species of tree and its edible seeds.
This intensely sour citrus hybrid — a cross between a kumquat and likely a mandarin orange — is a staple of Philippine cooking and also popular in Malaysian and Indonesian cuisine — which fruit?
Calamansi: Hybrid species of citrus. Calamansi (Citrus × microcarpa), also known as calamondin, Philippine lime, or Philippine lemon, is a citrus hybrid cultivated predominantly in the Philippines.
Extracted from the cochineal insect, this bright-red pigment is also known by the food-additive code E120 — what is it called?
Carmine: Pigment, aluminium salt of carminic acid.
The biochemist hailed as the "father" of industrial fermentation, instrumental in the 1917 Balfour Declaration, became the first president of Israel — who was he?
Chaim Weizmann: Israeli statesman and British chemist (1874–1952)
Native to the Andean forests of South America, this genus of trees is nicknamed the 'fever tree' because its bark yields quinine, the only effective malaria treatment for centuries — what is it?
Cinchona: Genus of plants, source of quinine.
Making up a quarter to a third of all protein in mammals, this triple-helix fibrous protein needs vitamin C for its synthesis and gives structure to cartilage, tendons, and skin — what is it?
Collagen: Most abundant structural protein in animals.
Latin for 'raven,' this widely distributed bird genus includes crows and rooks and gave a group of its members the eerie collective noun 'a murder' — what genus is it?
Corvus: Genus of birds including crows, ravens and rooks.

First synthesized in 1874, this insecticide earned its discoverer a 1948 Nobel Prize and was used in WWII against malaria and typhus before becoming infamous for its environmental damage — what is it?
DDT: Organochloride known as an insecticide.

This group of microalgae generates roughly a fifth to a half of Earth's oxygen each year, and its dead shells drift on Saharan winds to fertilize the entire Amazon basin with millions of tons of dust annually. What are they?
Diatom: Single-celled alga with a silica cell wall.
Smaller and shorter-necked than their swan and goose cousins in the family Anatidae, these aquatic birds are often confused with grebes, loons, and coots — what are they?
Duck: Common name for many species of bird.
The first woman admitted to MIT, this environmental chemist was the first to apply chemistry to nutrition and founded the home economics movement — who was she?
Ellen Swallow Richards: American engineer and chemist (1843–1911)
The major female sex hormone, this estrogen drives the development of secondary sexual characteristics and helps maintain reproductive tissues from puberty through pregnancy — what is it?
Known for its smooth silvery-grey bark and toxin-laced but edible nuts, this deciduous tree native to Europe includes the striking copper-leaved cultivar among its ornamentals — which species?
Fagus sylvatica: Species of deciduous tree. It is native to much of Europe, growing in humid climates.
This normal, occasionally embarrassing bodily process brings intestinal gas to the rectum, pressurizes it with muscle contractions, and releases it through the anus — what is it?
Flatulence: Bodily function of expelling intestinal gas from the anus.
Marketed as Neurontin, this anticonvulsant and GABA derivative is prescribed for nerve pain and partial seizures by binding to the α2δ subunits of calcium channels — what is it?

Caused by excess growth hormone before a child's growth plates fuse — usually from a pituitary tumor — this rare disorder produces height at least three standard deviations above average. What condition is it?
Gigantism: Human growth disorder. It is a rare disorder resulting from increased levels of growth hormone before the fusion of the growth plate which usually occurs at some point soon after puberty.
One of the heaviest snakes alive, which non-venomous constrictor prefers shallow, slow-moving South American waters like flooded grasslands and rivers?
An English GP convicted in 2000 of murdering 15 patients, he's reckoned one of history's most prolific serial killers with an estimated 250 victims — who was he?
Harold Shipman: English doctor and serial killer (1946–2004)
The offspring of a stallion and a female donkey, this equine hybrid is the rarer reciprocal cross to the mule and was often mistaken in European folklore for a horse-cow hybrid — what is it?
Hinny: Domestic horse–donkey hybrid. It is the reciprocal cross to the more common mule, which is the product of a male donkey (a jack) and a female horse (a mare).
First made in Belgium in 1956 and sold under the brand names Atarax and Vistaril, this first-generation antihistamine also treats anxiety and insomnia — what drug?
Hydroxyzine: Antihistamine drug. It is used in the treatment of itchiness, anxiety, insomnia, and nausea (including that due to motion sickness).
This probability principle holds that a randomly typing creature, given endless time, would almost surely reproduce the complete works of Shakespeare — what's it called?
Infinite monkey theorem: Counterintuitive result in probability.

A Manhattan Project veteran, this American physicist won a share of the 1975 Nobel Prize for proposing that not all atomic nuclei are spherical — an idea later confirmed by Aage Bohr and Ben Mottelson. Who was he?
James Rainwater: American physicist. Rainwater joined the physics faculty at Columbia in 1946, where he reached the rank of full professor in 1952 and was named Pupin Professor of Physics in 1982.
Dubbed the 'Angel of Death,' this German physician held doctorates in both anthropology and medicine before joining the SS and selecting Auschwitz prisoners for the gas chambers — who was he?
Josef Mengele: Nazi SS doctor at Auschwitz (1911–1979)
Made from shredded pastry dough layered with cheese and soaked in sugar syrup, this Arab dessert is especially popular during Ramadan, with a famous variant hailing from Nablus — what is it?
This Hungarian-born physicist conceived the nuclear chain reaction in 1933, then drafted the letter Einstein signed that launched the Manhattan Project — who was he?
Leo Szilard: Hungarian-American physicist and inventor (1898–1964)

Born from a 1970s Skunk Works project to dodge Soviet missile defenses, this subsonic single-seat attack jet became the first operational aircraft ever designed around stealth technology, first flying in 1981 at Groom Lake — which aircraft is it?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: American stealth ground-attack aircraft.

Founder of the Kerala school, this Indian mathematician was the first to use infinite series to approximate trigonometric functions — a 'decisive step' toward the limit-passage to infinity; who is he?
Madhava of Sangamagrama: Indian mathematician and astronomer (1340–1425)
Growing out of calculus and the study of derivatives and integrals, this branch of mathematics examines functions, spaces, and limits using methods of approximation and convergence — which field?

Mathematical analysis: Branch of mathematics. Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
This scientific field studies the atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with applications spanning aviation, agriculture, and disaster management — what field is it?
Meteorology: Scientific study of the atmosphere focusing on weather forecasting.
Sold as Remeron, this atypical tetracyclic antidepressant is often chosen when depression comes tangled with anxiety or insomnia — which drug is it?
Mirtazapine: Antidepressant medication. Mirtazapine, sold under the brand name Remeron among others, is an atypical tetracyclic antidepressant, and as such is used primarily to treat depression.

Made of contractile proteins called actin and myosin, this soft tissue exists in three vertebrate forms — skeletal, cardiac, and smooth — and forms during a developmental process called myogenesis — what is it?
Muscle: Important Biological tissue that allows movement.
Named after a German physical chemist, this electrochemistry formula calculates a reaction's reduction potential from temperature, electron count, and reactant concentrations — which relationship?
Nernst equation: Physical law in electrochemistry.
Practitioners of this field are sometimes mistaken for mere coin collectors, but they study all means of paying debts — even the horses the Kyrgyz once used as currency. What's the field called?
Numismatics: Study of currencies, coins and paper money.
Described as far back as the 300s BC by Hippocrates, this bone infection most often strikes the spine in adults and the long bones in children — which condition?
Osteomyelitis: Infection of the bones. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.

Native to southern Brazil, Paraguay and northern Argentina, this vine produces a round berry that turns yellow or dark purple at maturity, prized for its juicy, seed-filled interior — what is it, scientifically speaking?
Passiflora edulis: Species of flowering plant in the passion flower family.
What is the process by which immune cells like macrophages and neutrophils engulf pathogens and debris with their plasma membrane, forming an internal compartment called a phagosome?
Phagocytosis: Cell membrane engulfing a large particle.
Used in randomized clinical trials as a genuine-looking but pharmacologically inert stand-in — like a sugar pill or saline shot — what's this sham treatment called?
Placebo: Substance or treatment of no therapeutic value.
This rare genetic disorder linked to chromosome 15 leaves affected children constantly hungry, often leading to obesity, alongside a narrow forehead and small hands and feet — what is it?
Prader–Willi syndrome: Genetic disorder involving an imprinted genomic region.
Studied by Confucius and central to rhetoric in ancient Greece and Rome, this skill involves delivering an address to a live audience — what is it called?
Public speaking: Performing a speech to a live audience.

The largest of the true foxes and the most widely distributed carnivore on Earth, this Northern Hemisphere native is so destructive where it's been introduced that it made the list of the world's 100 worst invasive species — which animal is it?
Red fox: Species of mammal. The red fox (Vulpes vulpes) is the largest of the true foxes, and the most widely distributed member of the order Carnivora.
The wild ancestor of the domestic pigeon, this pale grey bird has two black bars on each wing and gave rise to feral pigeons worldwide — what is it?
Rock dove: Ancestor of domestic pigeon. The domestic pigeon, often called "Columba livia domestica", which includes about 1,000 different breeds, is descended from this species.

A member of the mint family native to the Mediterranean, this grayish-leaved perennial subshrub is used both in cooking and as an ornamental garden plant — which herb, better known by its common name sage?
Salvia officinalis: Species of plant. Salvia officinalis, common sage or sage, is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.
Encompassing several superfamilies and families, this taxonomic order groups together cephalopods that each have ten arms — which order is it?
These slow-moving South American mammals hang upside down in rainforest canopies, are kin to anteaters, and — despite the "two-toed" label — all have three toes on each rear limb; what are they?
Sloth: Group of tree dwelling mammals noted for slowness.
The sole living member of its genus, this slender, long-legged antelope of southwest Africa sports a white face, a dark eye-to-mouth stripe, and backward-curving horns on both sexes — what is it?
Springbok: Antelope of southwest and south Africa. The springbok or springbuck (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.
Described as the most economically important oxide of its element, this compound with the formula SO3 is a key precursor to sulfuric acid and to acid rain — what is it?
Sulfur trioxide: Chemical compound. Sulfur trioxide exists in several forms: gaseous monomer, crystalline trimer, and solid polymer.

Named after the mathematician who introduced it in 1715, this infinite sum built from a function's derivatives at a single point becomes a special case named for Colin Maclaurin when centered at zero — what is it?
Taylor series: Mathematical approximation of a function.
Colored metallic blue on top and silvery below for camouflage, this genus of warm-blooded ocean fish includes the giant Atlantic bluefin and eight of the true tuna species — what genus is it?
Thunnus: Genus of fishes. Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Known as a noxious weed for its spiky, woody burs that can puncture bare feet and even bicycle tires, this invasive desert-loving plant is native to Eurasia and Africa — name the species?
Tribulus terrestris: Species of flowering plant. Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
This hormone-responsive organ nourishes a developing embryo and fetus until birth, connecting at its narrow lower end to the cervix and at its upper corners to the fallopian tubes — what is it?
Uterus: Female sex organ in mammals.
Usually appearing on the hands and feet due to a human papillomavirus infection, this benign skin growth typically clears on its own within months to years — what is this common growth called?
Wart: Small, rough growth resembling a cauliflower or a solid blister.
Known as the 'grunting ox,' this long-haired domesticated bovine roams the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayan region, descended from a wild ancestor called Bos mutus — what animal is it?
The symbol for silver is Ag. Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag and atomic number 47.
The symbol for mercury is Hg.
